_comment: ArkPanel configuration. READ_ONLY blocks every mutating endpoint - it stays true until the Phase 2 ini round-trip gate and Phase 3 launch model are proven.

panel._comment: behind_proxy: set true when something terminates TLS in front of the panel (Tailscale serve, nginx, Cloudflare). Behind a proxy every request appears to come from 127.0.0.1, so the loopback exemption in the auth check would hand the whole network an unauthenticated control surface. It only matters if panel_user/panel_password are unset, but that is exactly when it would bite.
panel._comment_embedded_agent: embedded_agent: the panel hosts this machine's own agent in-process, so a single-PC install is one program. Other PCs run the standalone agent and join the cluster. When true the separate 'ArkPanel Agent' scheduled task MUST be stopped - both would run a scheduler, a monitor and a Discord watcher against the same servers and the same bot token.

backup._comment: Versioned save snapshots. Enabled by default because retiring DSM removed a backup layer. local_keep 4 (was 18) since 2026-11-11: the user keeps the SSDs for speed-critical things only, and every snapshot is also copied to external_root on I: (keep 84), so the local copies are only for quick restores. Each snapshot is ~1.75 GB.

schedule._comment: Disabled until you have watched a manual restart work and want it unattended. An automatic restart is disruptive enough to be an explicit choice.
schedule.warn_message: Server restarting in {minutes} minutes - log out safely and do NOT transfer between maps until it is back

monitor._comment: Health checks. Detect and alert only - nothing here restarts a server. DSM's crash detection restarted a healthy server off a false positive, and an auto-restart driven by a bad reading is worse than the fault it thinks it is fixing.

updates._comment: enabled = poll Steam and report. auto_apply = actually patch when a build lands. stagger = patch one map at a time and STOP if one fails, so a failure never takes the whole cluster down. settle_minutes = wait this long after first seeing a new build before patching, because Steam publishes the build id before the content is reliably downloadable; raise it if patches keep failing on the first attempt, lower it to get updates sooner. A manual/forced update ignores settle_minutes.

autostart._comment: Start this PC's servers again after an unattended reboot - power loss, Windows update. Gated on boot_window_seconds since the machine booted, so restarting the agent to deploy code never resurrects a server that was stopped on purpose. delay_seconds is on top of the boot task's own 90s delay. Set a server's own "autostart": false to exclude it.

discord._comment: info_channels: Discord channel ids Guardian keeps up to date. It posts its own messages and EDITS them - it cannot edit posts a human wrote, so the original hand-written ones must be deleted by hand. info_refresh_hours: how often to re-render and push if anything changed. control_channel: where Guardian posts the button control panel. control_role_ids: Discord ROLE ids allowed to press those buttons - the owner is always allowed, and an empty list means owner only, which is the safe default for buttons that can stop a server. palworld_channel: the #palworld channel - Guardian keeps the how-to-join post and the game-switch buttons there.

live_status._comment: Guardian keeps a live status embed for servers whose PC runs no watcher bot of its own - his three maps. Same channel and layout as the two watchers. channel: the cluster-status channel id.
live_status.label: his PC

game_channels._comment: STANDARD for a non-ARK game channel: add the game here with its channel id and Guardian keeps it holding a how-to-join post (the game adapter's discord_info) plus one live status embed with Start/Stop/Restart/Refresh, updated every minute and republished on panel start. The game must also be enabled in its own config block. Palworld predates this and uses palworld_channel.

palworld._comment: A Palworld server sharing PC1's memory with the Island - only one runs at a time, which is what the switch is for. On UDP 7777. NOTE: the claim that PC1 has 7000-7999 forwarded is UNVERIFIED and is now doubtful - UDP 7300 was tested from cellular on 2026-10-23 and did not answer. Whether 7777 reaches the internet has never actually been tested; do not rely on it without checking. Community server (-publiclobby) so the Xbox can find it in the in-game list; it cannot join by IP. RCON uses the cluster rcon_password from secrets.json and must never be forwarded. task_name: the scheduled task that OWNS the server process - launched any other way it dies with whatever started it, which corrupted the world twice. backup_root: versioned save snapshots, taken on every start and stop; the game's own backup folder only holds ~2 days. restart_time: a nightly restart, which it never had - 16 days of uptime grew it 0.85 GB -> 2.04 GB and pushed it into the page file, which is what made parachutes drift up and pals teleport. 05:00 because nobody is on then.
palworld.moved_to: HOME-SERVER-2 (C:\ASA-Server-2\Palworld, UDP 8010) on 2026-11-09 - PC1 install kept as fallback

sdtd._comment: 7 Days to Die. Telnet console, not Source RCON. ServerPort is set into PC1's already-forwarded 7000-7999 UDP range rather than opening 26900-26902 on the router. Telnet is loopback only and must never be forwarded.
sdtd._crossplay_note: Game Pass / Xbox clients reportedly join through EOS crossplay, which needs a PUBLIC, vanilla, EAC-enabled dedicated server. Sources are hosting guides and conflict, so this is a hypothesis to test by joining, not a documented fact.

minecraft._comment: Minecraft Bedrock. Free official server from Mojang - no Steam. No remote console exists, so status comes from a RakNet ping and stopping uses CTRL_BREAK so the world saves. MEASURED 2026-10-23: UDP 7300 at the public IP does NOT answer from outside - tested from a phone on cellular. The 7000-7999 range is NOT forwarded for UDP, whatever was assumed before. Remote access goes over Tailscale (PC1 is 100.64.0.99), which needs no router change and exposes nothing.

autoupdate._comment: Minecraft clients auto-update and the server does not, so a Mojang release locks everyone out of a server that still looks healthy. Checked against Mojang's own download API. Never applied while players are online; the pre-update snapshot must succeed first; server.properties, allowlist.json and permissions.json are preserved because Mojang's zip ships its own and an empty allowlist with allow-list=true refuses everybody.

bedrockconnect._comment: Lets an Xbox reach a self-hosted Minecraft server. BedrockConnect is the menu; core/bedrockdns.py is the DNS that sends the console to it. LAN-ONLY on purpose - exposing DNS to the internet would route every lookup from whoever points at it through this PC.
